question: How much does measured low-MIC classification change when assay rows, peptide sequences, papers or joint source/sequence components define evaluation folds?
source: public positive-only assay table, pinned to commit 5ac295c08f48aef43c991ba40a706f0e2fedb5b7
endpoint: reported MIC <= 16 uM; label only exact values or censoring bounds that determine this event
negative_class: above the MIC threshold, not biologically inactive
exclusions: mass units without chemistry-specific molecular weight
classifier: StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C=1, class_weight=balanced, max_iter=2000); fit independently inside each fold
fold_construction: Canonicalize grouped partitions by sorted member row IDs, so group renaming cannot change fold assignment; split algorithms and model settings are not chosen for performance.
uncertainty: 2000 paper-block bootstrap replicates over fixed out-of-fold predictions; this is not uncertainty from retraining
comparisons: descriptive; changing group constraints changes training distributions as well as overlap
claim_boundary: Pooled organisms, retrospective source data and positive-only selection prevent interpretation as a deployable antimicrobial classifier. No significance or field-first claims are planned.
